gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how far the GardePro Link 1.0 reaches in actual woods: about 384 ft (117 m) in GardePro's own dense-forest test, roughly a quarter of the 1,600 ft 'typical' figure that Magnolia repeats, and about 885 ft in light timber.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages. Magnolia Trail Camera gives only Link 1.0's 1,600 ft typical rating and its own 100–150 ft outdoor reach for a home router, with no prices and no range by terrain. The GardePro E8 3.0 Pro docs page gives only the 165 ft direct-connect range and no home-Wi-Fi range. The GardePro E9 3.0 Pro product page (via the store feed) gives the 7,800 mAh battery and the 30 m night vision. None of them has range by terrain, a share of the rated range, solar refill time or a side-by-side price.
decides: It sharpens ChatGPT's follow-up question about distance from the house. In thick brush, Link 1.0's tested ~384 ft is about 2.6–3.8× the 100–150 ft outdoor router reach that Magnolia cites. So for a camera in timber beyond about 150 ft, the Link 1.0 is the pick, but the shopper should plan around ~384–885 ft, not 1,600 ft. Within router range, the E8 3.0 Pro and E9 3.0 Pro both cost $119.99 at GardePro on 2026-11-10, so price doesn't separate them.

findings.note: GardePro in-house test, 'Extreme (Thick Brush)', standard 2 dB antenna, 1.5 m mounting height, article dated 2026-03-13. 384 ft ÷ 1,600 ft = 0.24. Maker's own test, not independent.

findings.label: Range in light timber and through buildings

findings.source_title: GardePro Link 1.0: Real-World Transmission Range Test Results
findings.note: GardePro in-house test, 'Moderate (Light Canopy)' and 'Heavy (Buildings/Walls)'. 885 ÷ 1,600 = 55% and 597 ÷ 1,600 = 37% of the typical rating. The same page quotes TrailCamPro at 2,100 ft rural in dense timber and 1,440 ft urban.

findings.label: Solar refill time at the panel's rated current
findings.note: 7,800 mAh ÷ 1,520 mA (SP1000 max output current, 6.6 V) = 5.1 h. 7,800 mAh ÷ 530 mA (SP300) = 14.7 h. The SP300 figure is from https://gardepro.com/products/gardepro-3-5w-solar-panel-sp300. Both panels list E8 3.0 Pro and E9 3.0 Pro as compatible. This is full-sun hours at rated output and ignores conversion loss and charge taper. The battery voltage isn't published, so it isn't a Wh-based figure. Prices: SP1000 $55.30, SP300 $39.00.
